llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Carbon ink is treated as the deposited analyte/ink component. Its formulation, concentration, and molecular weight are not specified and are not needed for the requested fixed-volume drop-cast operation. Carbon ink must be available in a compatible source vial or pipetting reservoir for deposition; it is not represented as a liquid-pump reagent because the liquid pump is reserved for compatible bulk solvents and cannot be assumed to contain arbitrary ink formulations.
assumptions: Solid KCl is loaded and available in Quantos cartridge position 1.
Water is available as a pump-compatible solvent on liquid channel 1.

A cleanable and polishable 3 mm glassy carbon working electrode is installed and compatible with the electrochemical cell, despite glassy carbon not being listed among the limited generic working-electrode examples in the schema.
Carbon ink is physically available in an accessible source container and the platform has a calibrated pipetting/deposition operation capable of delivering 10 uL.
A platinum wire counter electrode and Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) aqueous reference electrode are installed, functional, and compatible with the aqueous KCl cell.

No nitrogen purge is performed because nitrogen availability was not specified and the requested initial potential limit of -0.20 V versus Ag/AgCl avoids intentionally driving strong oxygen reduction. Dissolved oxygen may still contribute background current near the negative limit.
The expected current magnitude of the carbon coating is unknown; AUTO current range is required to prevent an avoidable range-selection error.
The 1800 second drying time is an ambient-drying assumption and must be confirmed by post-deposition camera inspection before the CV measurement.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: For 0.10 M KCl in 15.0 mL: required moles = 0.10 mol/L x 0.0150 L = 0.00150 mol. Using KCl molecular weight 74.5513 g/mol, mass = 0.00150 mol x 74.5513 g/mol = 0.11182695 g = 111.82695 mg. The planned Quantos mass is rounded to 111.83 mg. Actual concentration = (0.11183 g / 74.5513 g/mol) / 0.0150 L = 0.10000273 M, effectively 0.100 M.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: One solid reagent is used, which is within the maximum of eight Quantos solid cartridges. KCl mass is 111.83 mg, below the 200 mg capacity per cartridge. One liquid pump channel is used, within the maximum of four channels. Water volume is exactly 15.0 mL, matching the required final vial volume and ensuring electrode immersion. One experiment vial and one electrochemical slot are used, within platform limits. KCl is represented as a solid and water as a pump-compatible liquid. The requested platinum counter electrode and aqueous Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode are specified. The requested 3 mm glassy carbon working electrode and carbon ink deposition operation are required hardware/materials and must be installed and available before execution; the user-specified electrode differs from the limited generic electrode-type examples in the schema, so the user-specified glassy carbon electrode is retained.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: A 1800 second ambient drying period is specified to allow the 10 uL carbon-ink drop-cast film to dry before electrolyte contact. This duration is a conservative operational assumption because the ink solvent composition and manufacturer-recommended drying protocol were not supplied. If camera inspection shows a visibly wet, mobile, cracked, or non-adherent film after 1800 seconds, the run must not proceed until the coating is dry and intact.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: Before deposition, polish the 3 mm glassy carbon working electrode for one polishing cycle, then wash and dry it. Pipette 10 uL carbon ink onto the electrode face by drop casting. Keep the electrode level to minimize uneven film thickness. Following drying, inspect the electrode with the platform camera to confirm coating coverage, absence of visible pooling or cracking, and acceptable film adhesion before immersion in the prepared KCl electrolyte.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense 111.83 mg solid KCl from Quantos cartridge position 1 into one 20 mL experiment vial. Dispense 15.0 mL water through liquid channel 1 into the same vial. Mix with a stir bar for 300 seconds to dissolve KCl completely and form approximately 0.100 M KCl. No pre-prepared electrolyte is assumed.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.10 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte was selected because it provides adequate ionic conductivity and reduced solution resistance while remaining well below the 200 mg single-cartridge Quantos limit for a 15 mL preparation. The requested potential window is implemented exactly as a scan from -0.20 V to +0.80 V versus Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl). A moderate 50 mV/s scan rate is selected for initial carbon-film characterization because it provides a practical compromise between measurement time, capacitive-current resolution, and film stability. A 5 mV potential increment provides 200 points over the 1.00 V forward sweep, sufficient to resolve broad capacitive and surface redox features. Exactly 10 cycles are specified as required; comparison of early and late cycles can indicate carbon-film conditioning, wetting, adhesion, or instability. AUTO current range is selected because the current response of the unspecified carbon ink film is not known in advance.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The experiment is analyte_on_working_electrode because carbon ink is deposited as a 10 uL film on the working electrode rather than dissolved in the electrolyte. The electrolyte is separately prepared in the experiment vial from solid KCl and water before the coated electrode is immersed.

metadata.description: Prepare 15 mL of 0.10 M aqueous KCl supporting electrolyte, drop-cast 10 uL carbon ink onto a 3 mm glassy carbon working electrode, dry the coating, and perform exactly 10 cyclic-voltammetry cycles from -0.20 to +0.80 V versus Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl).
metadata.experiment_name: Carbon-ink-coated glassy-carbon electrode CV in 0.10 M KCl
metadata.user_prompt: Perform CV to characterize carbon deposited (10 uL) onto a glassy carbon working electrode (d = 3 mm). Pipette the carbon ink onto the electrode and allow it to dry. Prepare 15 mL of KCl supporting electrolyte using available solid KCl and water. Immerse the coated electrode and perform CV using a platinum counter electrode and Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode. Select a suitable KCl concentration and justified CV settings, starting with a potential window of -0.2 to +0.8 V versus Ag/AgCl and exactly 10 cycles. Verify reagent and hardware availability, follow safety requirements, and return the complete executable configuration in the required JSON schema.

cross_contamination_risks: Carbon ink can contaminate polishing stations, electrode holders, pipetting tools, vial rims, and subsequent experiments.
KCl residue can contaminate non-aqueous or chloride-sensitive experiments; perform wash-and-dry operations after the run.
Avoid transferring KCl electrolyte into the Ag/AgCl reference-electrode filling solution or onto the reference junction exterior.
handling_precautions: Wear laboratory coat, safety glasses, and suitable nitrile gloves when loading KCl, handling carbon ink, and assembling electrodes.
Load dry KCl into the assigned Quantos cartridge and avoid moisture uptake or cross-contamination.
Polish and rinse the glassy carbon electrode before carbon-ink deposition; do not polish after the ink has been deposited.
Drop-cast exactly 10 uL carbon ink onto the electrode surface, keep the electrode level during drying, and prevent contact with the active coated area.
Allow the coating to dry for 1800 seconds before immersion; use camera inspection to confirm that the film is visibly dry, adherent, and confined to the electrode face.
Ensure the working, counter, and reference electrodes are immersed without physical contact or shorting.
hazards: Potassium chloride is a low-hazard inorganic salt; avoid ingestion and contact with eyes.
Carbon ink composition is unspecified and may contain volatile solvent, conductive carbon particulates, binders, or surfactants; handle according to its SDS.
Platinum counter electrode, glassy carbon electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode are fragile and may have sharp components.
Electrical and pinch hazards apply during automated dispensing, stirring, polishing, and potentiostat operation.
waste_disposal: Collect used KCl electrolyte, carbon particles, carbon ink residues, and electrode-rinse liquids in the designated aqueous electrochemical waste stream unless the carbon-ink SDS requires organic or hazardous-solvent waste handling.
Do not dispose of carbon ink or electrolyte containing carbon particles down the drain.
Clean electrode holders and dispensing tools using the approved wash procedure between experiments to avoid carbon carryover.
